definition.interpretation: The initial gridworld experiment yielded a policy divergence of ~0.13, which failed to meet the significance threshold (>=0.20) established in hyp-mem-pref-01. This suggests either the memory mechanism requires longer temporal horizons to manifest preference bias, or the gridworld task lacks the structural complexity to differentiate agent trajectories based on history.
definition.limitations: The observed divergence was statistically weak, and the simulation duration (2000 episodes) may be insufficient for path-dependent preferences to coalesce in the chosen architecture.
definition.next_step: Implement a modified gridworld experiment with a longer episode horizon and stochastic noise reduction to isolate path-dependent bias.

definition.method: Execute a comparative gridworld simulation where Agent A uses a recurrent memory buffer (long-term history) and Agent B uses a Markovian state representation (immediate state only). Increase episode horizon by 5x compared to exp-mem-pref-04 to observe long-term policy stabilization.
definition.stop: Completion of 10,000 episodes or significant policy stabilization.
definition.success: Observe sustained policy_divergence >= 0.20 over the final 500 episodes.

proposal.summary: Interpreting inconclusive experiment results for memory-augmented agents and proposing a refined simulation protocol to isolate path-dependent divergence in deterministic environments.
proposal.title: Refining Path-Dependent Preference Experiments
